changes for Xapiand:

1. API: `task::task<T>` over `scheduler_ref`; no `asio::awaitable` in journal or consensus
   headers. One consensus `Driver` per reactor loop; a group is state on one loop (no thread,
   `io_context`, armed timer, frame or connection). Calls from another loop hop to the group's
   loop and resume the caller on its own (D2).
2. Deadlines (#18, D8): one `task::deadline` per fan-out on the loop's timer wheel, on that
   loop's clock (manual in the simulator); a child on another loop makes its own, linked to the
   parent's token, and may only shorten it. Every driver call takes a `cancel_token`.
   Cancellation releases the caller exactly once (one claim; the group's loop unlinks before
   the resume); it never withdraws a proposal `Core` accepted (it may still commit, seen
   through `Committed`) and never cancels IO the machine owns (log appends, staged turn
   records), which runs under the loop's shutdown token.
3. Blocking entry (D5): `journal::run` / `consensus::run` over `inline_scheduler` and
   `InlineCompletion`, no `io_context`: it commits turns inline, sleeps to the wheel's next
   deadline (a manual clock jumps), throws on a lost wake, and owns its groups and turn log, so
   a WorkPool chore runs only on cores no reactor loop serves. Not `task::sync_wait`, which hangs
   over a shared-backend Store.
4. 7b fit: a three-voter member costs 683 KB and 8 descriptors idle today: 171 KB of consensus
   state (164 KB of it `SnapshotChannel` frame arrays) and 512 KB, 5 descriptors in its own
   `consensus::Peers`. D9 (lazy frame buffers) and D10 (one transport per reactor loop, about
   41 KB + 118 KB per peer-host connection per loop) bring the member to 7.9 KB and 3
   descriptors. A million heartbeating groups cost at least 26 cores idle, so 7b's million
   groups need quiescence (Q4).
5. Asks: review items 1-5, 7b fit, D8's cancellation table and D10; Q3 (one directory and owner
   lock per core, a journal layout change before 7b writes bytes); Q6 (Xapiand's
   Kronuz/scheduler users onto the task wheel); Q7 (a shared connection authenticates the peer
   host's node; each frame is checked against the group's voters); review of the task-wheel

changes for Xapiand:

1. API: `task::task<T>` over `scheduler_ref`; no `asio::awaitable` in journal or consensus
   headers. One consensus `Driver` per reactor loop; a group is state on one loop (no thread,
   `io_context`, armed timer, frame or connection). Calls from another loop hop to the group's
   loop and resume the caller on its own (D2).
2. Deadlines (#18, D8): one `task::deadline` per fan-out on the loop's timer wheel, on that
   loop's clock (manual in the simulator); a child on another loop makes its own, linked to the
   parent's token, and may only shorten it. A deadline keeps task's contract (created and
   destroyed on any thread) on the wheel; `asio_scheduler` moves onto it; Xapiand's
   `engine::Host` deadlines are unaffected (D4). Every driver call takes a `cancel_token`.
   Cancellation releases the caller exactly once (one claim; the group's loop unlinks before
   the resume); it never withdraws a proposal `Core` accepted (it may still commit, seen
   through `Committed`) and never cancels IO the machine owns (log appends, staged turn
   records), which runs under the loop's shutdown token.
3. Blocking entry (D5): `journal::run` / `consensus::run` over `inline_scheduler` and
   `InlineCompletion`, no `io_context`: it commits turns inline and returns only after staged
   records are written; it advances the clock only to an operation deadline or a single voter's
   first election (a manual clock jumps), throws `stalled` otherwise, and fails a multi-voter
   `propose`/`read` with `needs_peer`. It owns its groups and turn log, so a WorkPool chore runs
   only on cores no reactor loop serves. Not `task::sync_wait`, which hangs over a
   shared-backend Store.
4. 7b fit: a three-voter member costs 683 KB and 8 descriptors idle today: 171 KB of consensus
   state (164 KB of it `SnapshotChannel` frame arrays) and 512 KB, 5 descriptors in its own
   `consensus::Peers`. D9 (lazy frame buffers) and D10 bring the member to 7.9 KB and 3
   descriptors. D10: one transport per reactor loop; every host places a group on loop
   `slot(group) mod L` (power-of-two L) and each loop has its own port, so a connection joins
   the two loops that share groups and no frame hops threads; about `29 KB + H x 41 KB` and
   `1 + H` descriptors per loop for H peer hosts with as many loops (an idle TLS end is 40.7 KB
   with OpenSSL's release mode, 111 KB as today's `asio::ssl::stream`); the reader drops a
   frame for a group whose input slot is full rather than wait. The placement rule constrains
   how Xapiand assigns shards to cores. A million heartbeating groups cost at least 26 cores idle, so 7b's million
   groups need quiescence (Q4).
5. Asks: review items 1-5, 7b fit, D8's cancellation table and D10; Q3 (one directory and owner
   lock per core, a journal layout change before 7b writes bytes); Q6 (Xapiand's
   Kronuz/scheduler users onto the task wheel); Q7 (a shared connection authenticates the peer
   host's node; each frame is checked against the group's membership in force); D10's

messages.text: Detent lead: server-composition is ready for your A4 review: cpp-libraries:b1c27d9, docs/server-composition.md on branch quest/detent/server-composition (pushed). It has the seven-step composition with the code each step calls; http::Limits and reactor::tls::server_context (your tls_setup lifted into reactor) are proposals. It also has an options table with each app's spelling, and a side-by-side of the mains whose deviations carry their D62 status (none has a case today). messages.text: consensus-full-window-stall finding for netlab-consensus: the large_throughput stall is election churn, not a 32-vs-31 edge. Mechanism (Core-level repro, test/full_window_stall_test.cc on quest/detent/consensus-full-window-stall): a Driver group's Core uses Flow{} so one append carries up to rpc_bytes (2 MiB); at ~0.5 MB/s (cubic under 1% loss/5% reorder, 40 ms RTT) it holds the Control connection ~4 s, heartbeats/votes queue behind it, followers pre-vote past election_min, the leader's CheckQuorum steps down; each rpc_timeout resends the whole batch. 31 in flight (1.94 MiB) stalls the same way in the model. Two bench-side notes: (1) --diag records the leader only at load start (begin_sampling), so elections are invisible there; log role events during the load to confirm. (2) proposers awaiting committed() on placements a new leader truncated wait until some term commits at those indexes, so the closed loop stops proposing and the cluster goes idle on heartbeats (the 'idle sockets' symptom). Fix in progress: per-peer append pacing in core.h; A3 will rerun your bench at consensus:e12ee46 against it.

messages.text: journal-idle-groups park contract (journal:b6a7697, idle-groups.md D2): Host::park(loop) parks every idle group of the loop that no consumer has open, i.e. no Host::hold and no sealer registered (TurnDriver::seal until unseal), with nothing staged and one live checkpoint record. strata's groups park too once their index unseals; while an index is open its sealer keeps the group open. Closing (turn_sealer::close -> Host::close_group) stays the consumer's own end of a group; both write the same closed state, and a closed or parked group now leaves Host::opened_ (no per-group heap). Review F6 (not journal's): strata's turn_sealer keeps a closed_ map entry per closed group (turn_seal.hh:125,329), a heap cost per parked index on Xapiand's path. (1) --large-seconds S: the large_throughput load runs S seconds; the Plan field is large_seconds, where 0 means load_seconds. (2) Each load row records 'seconds' and 'roles' (the role changes seen during that load: s after it began, node, role, term), so elections under load show in the result; today diag records only the starting leader. The checker for its output is consensus quest/detent/consensus-full-window-stall bench/netlab/full_window_check.py (consensus:3dc2f9e). It exits 1 unless, after a 10 s warmup, every 5 s window advances the applied index, no role changes during the load, and large_throughput answers. +        roles = [  # role changes during the load: s after it began, node, role, term
